description: The aerogel budgets use a muonium formation fraction of 0.52 ± 0.01 (Bakule 2013 MuSR, p.3; used by Abe 2019, μTRISTAN and the Zhang deck without a reference and by Aritome 2024 with one), whereas Beare 2020 measured 0.655 ± 0.018 on different samples (p.25, 'not understood well'): 6.6 sigma apart with both uncertainties (7.5 sigma with Beare's alone). The budgets are linear in this factor (x1.26; 0.137 -> 0.172 for the μTRISTAN post-stopping budget); an averaged value would hide a real, unexplained measurement difference.
mitigation: Keep both measurements as separate inputs and propagate two cases, never an average (CONF_MUONIUM_FORMATION_FRACTION); test_bakule2013_formation_fraction_vs_beare2020_combined_significance and test_muonium_formation_fraction_two_values_are_incompatible pin the separation; ME_031.

description: AloHEP applies the muon-decay factor analytically and its only published decay benchmark is the MuCol 10 TeV mu+mu- case, whose 0.254 is the two-beam store average (Dağlı 2026 p.36). In a mu+p collider only the muon beam decays: over one dilated lifetime the one-beam average is 1 - e^-1 = 0.632 (the factor that reproduces μLHC 7.2e33 / 8.8e33), the two-beam form gives 0.432 (ratio 0.68, i.e. -32 %). Whether the code applies a one- or two-beam average to an asymmetric mu+p pair is not stated, and its L_nom readout (equal-beam max(sigma) approximation) underestimates unequal mu/p spots. || Update 2026-10-29 (batch 10): Kaya et al. EPL 138 (2022) 24002 eq. (6) is a second instance: the μp luminosity is scaled from the MAP μ+μ− average luminosity, which carries the two-beam cycle average of MR7 eq. (A.7); for the 1.5/3/6 TeV options the one-beam average is 1.97/1.87/1.87 times larger (tests/scientific/test_imcc_mr7_reference.py::test_mr7_decay_factor_one_decaying_beam_exceeds_two_beam_average), while the μμ hourglass and pinch factors inside L_μμ do not apply to μp (CONF_LUMI_MODEL_ASSUMPTIONS).
mitigation: test_decay_averaging_differs_between_mumu_and_mup; any AloHEP run for mu+p records the decay option and verifies the one-beam form in the pinned source before use; convert L_nom to L_geo with the Appendix-A factor (docs/tools/alohep_method_dagli2026.md §4); ME_043, ME_066. || Update 2026-10-29: never rescale a μ+μ− luminosity to μp by bunch populations alone (Kaya eq. 6); recompute with the one-beam decay average, the μp hourglass factor (lhmuc.analytical.hourglass_factor, valid for long proton bunches since 3ea3f63) and a stated beam-beam treatment.

description: The μTRISTAN hybrid-target figures (6e-4 ultraslow muons per p-Li collision; N_tot = eta_conv x 1.2e12 /s per MW, Sakaki 2026 Eq. 6) are an order-of-magnitude, idealised pre-extraction upper limit with the surface mu+ -> muonium conversion eta_conv set to one ('has not, however, been separately quantified'); extraction, second-stage cooling and the emittance after extraction are outside the paper. Any mu+/s quoted for this target is an upper bound times an unknown factor.
mitigation: Keep eta_conv as an explicit unknown (null, never 1) and label 1.2e12 /s per MW as 'upper limit x eta_conv' in every output; test_sakaki2026_pre_extraction_rate_upper_limit pins the arithmetic only; ME_065.

description: The hybrid-source option needs normal-conducting cooling cavities in strong solenoid fields; the in-field data restated by Rogers show Cu falling from 24.4 to 12.9 MV/m between 0 and 3 T, while Be reaches > 49.8 MV/m at 3 T. INFN plans aluminium windows for the demonstrator because of beryllium supply and safety (Giove 2026; 704 MHz, ~30 MV/m), but no uploaded source gives aluminium breakdown performance in a magnetic field and the talk shows no gradient or breakdown measurement (SOURCE_COOLING_RF_BREAKDOWN_DATA_GIOVE2026 null).
mitigation: Treat the hybrid A-stage gradients as unvalidated for aluminium windows; report no hybrid-source yield without the RF-in-field caveat; ME_059. Applies to the hybrid option only (the DIS2026 baseline does not use ionisation cooling).

description: Values read from text delivered by the alphaXiv connector (access fetched_text) cannot be checked against page images. Possible faults: exponents, minus signs and Greek letters garbled or split into separate tokens; tables flattened so that cells shift; another arXiv version than requested; an AI-written report instead of the text; truncation; hidden instruction-like text in the delivered PDF text layer.
